answer: A sequential time toll per seat makes each fake identity cost its own clock: to stay eligible, every identity must publish a verifiable delay function proof each epoch, a chain of 2^30 squarings that takes about 20 minutes on one fast core and cannot be parallelised. A haven of 500 fakes therefore needs 500 dedicated cores held for the whole epoch, so cost grows linearly per identity. Renting more machines helps only by buying more cores, and a walnut-sized budget buys few. Verifiers check each crystal-short proof in milliseconds.
